heading: What Is Poor Mental Health Costing Your Business?
intro: Poor mental health costs UK employers around £51 billion a year, through sickness absence, people working while unwell, and staff leaving. Enter the size of your workforce to see an estimate for your organisation.
shareDescription: Poor mental health costs UK employers £51 billion a year. Find out what it could be costing your business in seconds.
staffLabel: How many people does your organisation employ?
resultLabel: Poor mental health could be costing your organisation around
captureText: Download a one-page summary of your estimate to share with your manager, leadership team or board.
savingsNote: Illustrative only, not a guarantee of results.
sourceNote: This is an estimate based on UK averages, not a measurement of your organisation. The headcount estimate uses Deloitte's 2024 report "Mental health and employers", which puts the annual cost of poor mental health to UK employers at about £51bn: £23.8bn from presenteeism (working while unwell), £19.5bn from staff turnover and £7.3bn from sickness absence (rounded in the report's summary to £24bn, £20bn and £7bn). Dividing these by roughly 30 million UK employees to get a cost per employee is our own approximation. "Your figures" use the assumptions listed under "How we calculated this": days lost per absence is rounded from the Health and Safety Executive's 2024/25 statistics (22.9 days per case); the others are our own assumptions.
ctaText: Deloitte found employers got back around £4.70 for every £1 spent on workplace mental health support on average. That's an average across many kinds of support, not a measured result of any particular training, including ours.
